default_rule.summary: Provincial (King's) highways are CLOSED to ORVs by default. O. Reg. 316/03 s.2: an ORV shall not be driven on any highway except as specified in Part II, permitted by Part IV, or crossing under ORVA s.2(2)(a). Schedule B lists the PERMITTED provincial highways (s.4(2)); Schedule A lists highways prohibited to all ORVs (s.3). An unlisted King's highway is prohibited (crossing only).

verbatim.s2: An off-road vehicle shall not be driven on any highway except, (a) as specified in this Part; (b) as permitted by Part IV; or (c) as permitted by clause 2 (2) (a) of the Off-Road Vehicles Act.
verbatim.s3: Except as permitted by section 28, no off-road vehicle shall be driven on a highway listed in Schedule A.
verbatim.s4: (1) Subject to subsection (2), no off-road vehicle shall be driven on a highway listed in Schedule B. (2) All-terrain vehicles, extreme terrain vehicles, multi-purpose off-highway utility vehicles, off-road motorcycles and recreational off-highway vehicles may be driven on a highway listed in Schedule B if the requirements of Part III are met.
verbatim.s4_1_1: An off-road vehicle shall not be driven on a highway or part of a highway that is under the jurisdiction of a municipality unless ... a by-law made by the council of the municipality under subsection 191.8 (3) of the Act permits the operation ... [ATV/UTV/ROV]; [XTV/ORM: by-law must specifically permit that class]; [by-law time limits apply]; The requirements of Part III are met.
verbatim.s4_1_2: Despite subsection (1), if the requirements of Part III are met, a vehicle described in paragraph 1 or 2 of subsection (1) may be driven on a highway or part of a highway that is under the jurisdiction of a municipality if the name of the municipality appears in the Table to Ontario Regulation 8/03 (Local Municipalities Where 80 Kilometres Per Hour Speed Limit Applies) made under the Act.
verbatim.s4_1_3: For greater certainty, an off-road vehicle driven on a highway in accordance with subsection (2) is subject to any applicable prohibition or limitation set out in a by-law made by the council of the local municipality under subsection 191.8 (3) of the Act.
verbatim.HTA_191_8_1: No person shall drive an off-road vehicle on a highway except in accordance with the regulations and any applicable municipal by-laws.

contradictions: ontario.ca guidance lists 'highways with low traffic volumes' as permitted; that is a description, not a legal test. Only Schedule B governs.

conditions.vehicle_types: Schedule B/s.4.1 permit: all-terrain vehicles (s.1 def: four wheels, handlebars, straddle seat, designed for 'a driver only and no passengers' [single-rider] or driver + one passenger with straddle seat behind and separate passenger footrests [two-up]), extreme terrain vehicles (6/8 wheels), multi-purpose off-highway utility vehicles (UTV), off-road motorcycles, recreational off-highway vehicles (ROV, <=1,000 cc). XTV/ORM on municipal roads need a by-law specifically permitting that class (s.4.1(1)2), but 8/03-listed municipalities allow 'paragraph 1 or 2' vehicles i.e. all five.
conditions.speed_s22: not greater than (a) 20 km/h if the posted limit is not greater than 50 km/h; (b) 50 km/h if the posted limit is greater than 50 km/h. Municipal by-laws may set lower (HTA 191.8(3)(c)).
conditions.position_s24: s.24(1) 'driven on the shoulder of the highway in the same direction as the traffic using the same side of the highway'; s.24(2) roadway allowed if no shoulder, shoulder obstructed, or shoulder not wide enough for all tires off roadway; s.24(3) roadway at level railway crossings; s.24(4)/(5) as close to right edge as practicable; s.24(7) not in median; s.24(8)-(9) not in construction zones/closed highways; s.24(10) no passing motor vehicles on same shoulder/roadway (may pass another ORV on shoulder, s.24(11)).
conditions.hours: No provincial hour restriction. Lamps: s.13(2) front white and rear red lamps 'must be lit at all times' on highway (off-road motorcycles only at night/poor visibility, s.13(2.1)). Municipal by-laws may restrict times (s.4.1(1)3).
conditions.permit_plate_s16: ORVA s.5 permit and number plate displayed.
conditions.insurance_s17: insured per Compulsory Automobile Insurance Act s.2 and ORVA s.15.
conditions.licence_s18: valid Class A, B, C, D, E, F, G, G2, M or M2 licence (so minimum age effectively 16; G1/M1 not allowed). G2/M2 under-20 passenger limits midnight-5 a.m. (s.18(2)-(3)).
conditions.helmet_s19: driver and every passenger wear helmet complying with ORVA s.19.
conditions.seatbelts_s19_1: UTV, ROV and XTV with belts: driver and passengers belted.
conditions.passengers: s.19.2 ATV passenger only if vehicle designed for driver+passenger and passenger straddles seat behind driver facing forward, feet on separate passenger footrests (so NO passengers on single-rider ATVs); s.19.3 no passenger under age eight on any ORV; s.19.4 no riders on trailer; s.19.5 no passengers on off-road motorcycles.
conditions.equipment: s.7-15: weight/width limits (UTV/XTV <=1,814 kg, ROV <=1,700 kg, width <=2.03 m), ANSI/COHV standard labels for post-2001 vehicles, brakes, lamps, reflectors, windshield, mirrors (UTV/ROV/XTV).
conditions.environment_s23: no harm to environment, fish habitat; no driving in watercourses on highway that harms fish habitat.
contradictions: ontario.ca guidance says headlights/tail lights 'mandatory at night and in bad weather'; the regulation s.13(2) requires them lit 'at all times' on a highway (except off-road motorcycles). Follow the regulation.

crossing.rule: ORVA R.S.O. 1990 c. O.4 s.2(2): 'Despite subsection (1), and section 7, subsection 32 (1) and subsections 62 (1), (3) to (26) and (28) to (32) of the Highway Traffic Act, a holder of a driver's licence issued under section 32 of the Highway Traffic Act who is not contravening any provision of this Act may drive an off-road vehicle, (a) directly across a highway; ...' O. Reg. 316/03 s.26: 'Part III of this Regulation does not apply to a person who drives an off-road vehicle directly across a highway pursuant to clause 2 (2) (a) of the Off-Road Vehicles Act.' s.2(2) does not apply to motorcycles with sidecar, farm tractors, etc. (s.2(3)). Schedule A highways: s.3 prohibits driving 'on' them; crossing permission in ORVA s.2(2)(a) is 'despite' HTA provisions, but s.3 of the reg has no crossing carve-out - treat 400-series/expressway crossings as not permitted except at road crossings (uncertain).
crossing.requirements: Driver's licence (any class), ORVA permit/plate (ORVA s.3), insurance (ORVA s.15), helmet (ORVA s.19), no ORVA contravention. Ontario guidance adds 'driver is at least 16 years old'.
sources: https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/030316 (consolidated from 2024-01-01, last amendment O. Reg. 176/22) s.26

parks.provincial_parks: O. Reg. 347/07 (Provincial Parks: General Provisions) s.34: 'No person shall operate an all-terrain vehicle in a provincial park except in an area operated by the superintendent for that purpose or in another area pursuant to a written authorization of the superintendent...' (ATV defined broadly to include any ORV under the ORVA). Also s.23(1) park permit required to take an ATV into a park; s.25(1) vehicles only on designated roadways. Hwy 60 through Algonquin additionally Schedule A item 29 of O. Reg. 316/03. O. Reg. 316/03 s.5 allows ORVs on highways within parks/conservation reserves 'unless ... prohibited by the road authority or is otherwise prohibited by law' - O. Reg. 347/07 s.34 is such a prohibition for park roads.
parks.conservation_reserves: O. Reg. 319/07 (Conservation Reserves: General Provisions) s.13(1): no motor vehicle except (b) a motor vehicle or ATV operated '(i) on an existing road or trail', (ii) off-trail for direct retrieval of legally harvested game, (iii) with written authorization; (c) ATV on frozen water. s.13(2) manager may prohibit on designated roads/trails. So ORVs ARE generally allowed on existing roads/trails in conservation reserves unless posted.
sources: https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/030316 (consolidated from 2024-01-01, last amendment O. Reg. 176/22) s.5

crown_land.rule: O. Reg. 316/03 s.5: 'An off-road vehicle may be driven on a highway or part of a highway that is on Crown land administered under the Public Lands Act ... unless the operation of the off-road vehicle on the highway or part of the highway is prohibited by the road authority or is otherwise prohibited by law.' Part III conditions (plate, insurance, licence, helmet, speeds) still apply on such roads. Public Lands Act R.S.O. 1990 c. P.43: s.28(1) Ministry may give notice (signs/media) prohibiting or controlling use of public lands or roads under the Minister's jurisdiction, offence s.28(3); s.52(1) district manager may close a road to the public or classes of the public (barricades, signs, internet notice), offence s.52(5); s.54(1) private forest roads not open to the public unless agreement. O. Reg. 239/13 concerns work permits and does not regulate ORV travel (checked: no vehicle provisions).
contradictions: ontario.ca guidance says on Crown land 'ride in designated areas only' and 'must always have the land owner's permission'; the law (s.5 + Public Lands Act) is permissive on Crown land roads unless closed/posted. The guidance is more restrictive than the statute text; app should present Crown roads as 'generally open unless posted/closed (PLA s.28/s.52)'.
sources: https://www.ontario.ca/laws/regulation/030316 (consolidated from 2024-01-01, last amendment O. Reg. 176/22) s.5

corrections_to_app: CRITICAL: App inverts Schedule B. Schedule B = PERMITTED highways (s.4(2)), not prohibited. Hwy 62 Hwy 7 (Madoc) -> 300 m S of Bay Lake Rd (app lat<45.045 'prohibited') is ALLOWED (B26).
Hwy 62: section from 300 m S of Bay Lake Rd through Bancroft to Hybla Rd is PROHIBITED (unlisted); Hybla Rd -> Hwy 127 (Maynooth) ALLOWED (B27); south of Hwy 7 prohibited.

Hwy 28: CR 504 (Apsley) -> Hwy 118 junction at Bancroft is ALLOWED (B16), not prohibited (app lon<-77.90 is wrong). The 'to a point in Faraday' wording belongs to Hwy 118 item B43. Bancroft core (118 jct -> 880 m E of Hastings St) PROHIBITED; 880 m E of Hastings St -> Hwy 41 (Denbigh) ALLOWED (B17); south of CR 504 PROHIBITED.

Hwy 118: ENTIRE highway ALLOWED (B3 lists No. 118 wholly; B42/B43 also). App's 'prohibited Bracebridge to Eagle Lake Rd (lon<-78.50)' is wrong - Eagle Lake Rd wording comes from pre-2015 B42 which was a PERMITTED segment.
Hwy 35: NOT all prohibited. ALLOWED B18 (200 m N of Horseshoe Lake Rd, Minden Hills -> Hwy 60, Lake of Bays) and B18.1 (S-most CR 121 jct -> 4300 m S of Deep Bay Rd). Rest prohibited by default.
Hwy 7: all prohibited in bbox is CORRECT (unlisted; A14 near Peterborough).

Hwy 60 through Algonquin Park prohibited is CORRECT (A29: 300 m S of Headstone Creek Bridge to Algonquin Highlands N boundary). But Hwy 60 outside the park in bbox is mostly ALLOWED (B21-B24: Renfrew County Horton -> Eganville -> Barry's Bay -> park east gate; park west gate -> Huntsville).

Hwy 127: ALLOWED entire (B3). Hwy 41: ALLOWED Bon Echo N boundary -> Foymount Rd (B19) and N of Eganville -> Hwy 17 (B20); else prohibited. Hwy 132: ALLOWED 1.5 km W of Lochiel Ave Renfrew -> Hwy 41 (B46). Hwys 37, 121, 17, 115 and Hwy 62 S of Madoc: PROHIBITED.
500-899: allowed is correct for provincial highways (B1), but most 5xx/6xx in bbox are now COUNTY roads (downloaded) and follow s.4.1 municipal rules (by-law or O. Reg. 8/03 listing).
7000-series: NOT blanket open. Only the specific numbers in B2 (all outside bbox). Any other 7000-series = prohibited by default.
'Other King's highways unconfirmed, shoulder only' is WRONG: unlisted King's highways are PROHIBITED (s.2). Shoulder rule (s.24) applies only where operation is permitted.

Municipal roads: in O. Reg. 8/03-listed municipalities (e.g. Faraday, Hastings Highlands, Wollaston, Limerick, Tudor and Cashel, Carlow/Mayo, Highlands East, Dysart et al, Minden Hills, North Kawartha, Madawaska Valley, South Algonquin...) roads are open by default since 2021-01-01 unless a by-law prohibits; Town of Bancroft is NOT listed - requires its own by-law.
Single-rider ATVs: may use permitted highways (s.1 def includes 'driver only and no passengers'), but must carry NO passenger (s.19.2).
